top_choice_rationale: P002 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson), with the citation anchored on the import-competition and local-labour-market evidence. This is the one strand where credit is a joint product of exactly these three people, so the three-name cap forces no arbitrary cut. The design answered a first-order question about who bears the cost of trade integration. It is transparent and has been replicated across countries. About a decade of scrutiny has refined magnitudes and exposed shift-share inference problems without overturning the qualitative finding. P001 (Kiyotaki and Moore) is a close second. It has the cleanest two-person attribution and nearly thirty years of influence, but its empirical validation is more indirect and its quantitative amplification is contested. I weigh direct evidence and clean attribution slightly above conceptual generality and age. I would accept P001 if the Committee puts maturity first. P003 is a substantial methodological advance with a defensible three-person core, but it depends more on functional-form and instrument assumptions and leaves out the wider structural-IO strand. Any of the three proposals is preferable to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: No co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Kiyotaki, Moore, Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn is apparent from my profile. I disclose that my work on capital-skill complementarity and technological change is adjacent to the skill-bias literature behind P002, and that my macroeconomics field is adjacent to P001. I co-author with Timo Boppart and John Hassler and am an IIES colleague of both. They are not candidates, although Hassler supports P001. These ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
